Hi Rachel — thanks for raising this. Short answer up front: billing records (invoices and the underlying financial ledger used for accounting) are retained for statutory and accounting reasons and are not removed as part of a standard DSR erasure request. However, there are established controls and limited remediation options we can use to address privacy concerns without deleting accounting-critical entries.

High-level notes:
- Accounting retention: Our finance policy requires us to retain invoice records and the usage ledger for tax and audit purposes (standard retention = 7 years in the US, subject to local variation).
- DSR vs. Ledger: A DSR asking for erasure of a user's personal data does not automatically remove aggregated usage or invoice line items that are necessary for financial record-keeping.
- PII redaction: Where an invoice or ledger line contains direct personal identifiers (email address, full name) that are not necessary for accounting, we can apply redaction or pseudonymization on a case-by-case basis.
- Legal hold / subpoenas: If there is an opposing legal hold or regulatory requirement, we may be required to preserve records beyond standard retention.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the exact identifier(s) Bellwether wants erased (user id vs. billing contact).
2) Finance (Neha) to confirm what can be redacted from the stored invoice PDF and ledger export without breaking audit trail.
3) Legal (Marissa) to confirm whether any contractual or regulatory obligations require preservation of the full identifier.

I'll loop Neha and Marissa into this thread to provide the precise finance/legal guidance and a recommended timeline (I expect a 3-5 business day turnaround for redaction assessment).

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel — Neha here from Finance. Wanted to confirm our practical approach and constraints.

What we can do:
- Invoice preservation: We cannot delete invoices or ledger entries that are required for financial reporting. Those records must remain intact in our accounting system and audit trail.
- Redaction/pseudonymization: We can produce a redacted version of an invoice PDF for display or customer-facing archives where direct PII (email, full name) is masked or replaced with a unique token/hash. This maintains the amounts, dates, invoice numbers, and resource IDs for audit while removing the end-user identifier from the visible copy.
- Ledger exports: For downstream accounting exports, we can pseudonymize the user identifier field but keep an internal mapping in a secure, access-controlled vault for authorized audit requests. The internal mapping is retained for auditability and is disclosed only under appropriate legal process.
- Reversibility: Full reversibility (i.e., recovering the original identifier from the redacted document) is possible only if the internal mapping exists and is accessible under controlled conditions. For pure deletion requests where a customer insists on full erasure of the mapping, we would not be able to reconstruct identifiers later. That would impact auditors' ability to reconcile individual transactions.

Timeline and required approvals:
- Redaction assessment: 1–3 business days to confirm fields and produce a redacted invoice PDF.
- Internal approvals: Legal sign-off required for any removal or pseudonymization of identifiers from historical records.

Attachments: redaction_guidelines.pdf (pdf) — contains steps and examples of what we can mask without breaking audit trails.

If Bellwether confirms you are comfortable with a pseudonymized invoice and with the auditors having controlled access to the mapping if needed, we can proceed and I will generate the redacted copy. Otherwise Marissa can advise on whether contractual obligations force us to retain the full identifier visible in records.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
